request.prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the wuum. Countless small bodies that all belong to one vast, spreading thing — every wuum you see is a cell of the same superorganism, working toward the same single purpose: grow, and keep growing. A wuum buds off a copy of itself every few days and needs almost nothing to eat. It bursts when it dies, and what bursts out burns like acid. Visible features it must show: a small soft body that looks like one cell of something larger; a bulbous budding outgrowth where it copies itself; acid-bright fluid glowing in chambers under a thin skin; a blob-like cellular form with the limbless, faceless body of a cell. Style: realistic, hand-painted vanilla RimWorld sprite with a thin, dark, painterly rim outline in a deep shade of the body colour running continuously around the whole silhouette and the budding outgrowth, so the shape reads clearly at standard zoom. The membrane is matte and layered with visible brush texture and painted shading; highlights are small and localized to a few spots. The luminous acid-filled chambers glow inside a firmly defined, more opaque membrane edge, so the contour is stronger than the interior glow in every facing. Keep the same palette and body plan as the previous render. Exactly ONE creature, centred, the whole body visible with nothing cut off. Fully transparent background: no ground, no water, no shadow, no text, no border.
